newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs edge up, other sectors flat.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs edge up, other sectors flat.

text.p: Very large crude carrier (VLCC) freight rates from the Middle East Gulf edged up on Wednesday with voyages to around year highs, brokers said.
Mideast/Japan voyages firmed to W76/77.5 from W75 with trips to other eastern destinations achieving at least as much.
The 260,000 tonne Delos fetched W77.5 for PTT on a voyage to Thailand and the Front Lady achieved the same rate to South Korea for Hyundai.
Trips to the west also firmed by about 2.5 points to W65.
"There's a bit more activity...It's down to the usual suspects -- supply and demand," said one broker, commenting on the rise.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCCs were quiet, with W65 still holding for now, while 130,000 tonne vessels (Suezmaxes) were lacklustre at W82.5/85, brokers said.
Cross-Med Suezmaxes were also in the doldrums at W80/85, they added.
The Aframax (80,000 tonne) market likewise remained soft, with inter-U.K./Cont trips continuing around the W100 level and cross-Med voyages at W120.
In the Western hemisphere, dirty rates were slightly softer, with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes at W120 and likely to fall further, and 50,000 tonne fuel oil stems at W160, brokers said.
European fuel was unchanged with 25,000 tonne cargoes in the Med at W180 and at W210 in the north. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
